answer: To curb Sybil attacks in agent markets%2C each participant must lock a non-trivial stake of native tokens before acting. The stake sits behind a verification ridge that only genuine sequential history can cross%3B an attacker spinning up thousands of identities would need a ferrous supply of capital equal to the number of fakes times the minimum lock%2C quickly exhausting any budget. A quill signature from the agent's long-term key further binds the deposit%2C making mass forgery prohibitively expensive.
